data.title: Not Found Page
data.tagline: Return 404 for a missing resource and give people a way to recover
data.learningOutcome: You can check whether an unknown URL really returns 404 and distinguish an error page from a flow result or redirect.
data.description: When an article link no longer works, the server should return 404, explain that the content was not found, and offer a list or search path. A Not Found message alone is not enough: Network must also show HTTP 404. If the content moved to a new address, use a redirect instead.

learning.assumes: You have opened a broken link or seen a request status in a browser's Network panel.
learning.outcome: You can check whether an unknown URL really returns 404 and distinguish an error page from a flow result or redirect.

explanation.title: The status tells systems the resource is missing
explanation.text: The server returns 404 for an unknown URL so browsers and search systems know the request found no resource. The page can be friendly, but it should not pretend success with 200.

explanation.title: Recovery links help people continue
explanation.text: A list, site search, or parent-page link can help people continue. The path should relate to the missing content instead of silently sending every error to the home page.

data.boundary: A not-found page handles a missing resource. A Result page reports success, failure, or processing after a flow ends. A Redirect changes the destination when an old URL has a matching new one. An empty list is not 404 because the list exists; it simply has no current items.

lessonPractice.title: An unknown article URL shows a Not Found message, but Network reports 200. What should happen next?

options.label: Return 404 for the URL while keeping the explanation and a link back to the article list
options.feedback: Correct. The page message and HTTP status should describe the same missing resource, with a recovery path for the user.

options.label: Turn it into a result page that says Operation failed and offers a resubmit button
options.feedback: No completed submission flow exists here, and retrying cannot create a missing article. The first problem is the resource and status mismatch.

options.label: Redirect every unknown URL to the home page and keep returning a success status
options.feedback: Sending unrelated URLs to the home page loses context and hides that the resource is missing. Redirect only when a matching replacement exists.

data.agentPrompt: Make unknown article URLs return HTTP 404 with a clear not-found page, a link back to the article list, and a search entry. Check the status in Network and then test the recovery links. If an article only moved, redirect its old URL to the matching new page instead.
